name: Handling Water Damage and Mold Discovered During a Bathroom Overhaul

mainEntity.name: What questions should I ask a Los Angeles County bathroom overhauling contractor about water damage and mold discovered during demolition?
mainEntity.text: What questions should I ask a Los Angeles County bathroom overhauling contractor about water damage and mold discovered during demolition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Water damage and possible mold are common discoveries once an old bathroom is opened. When your contractor encounters these issues, you need a clear plan rather than rushed decisions. Start by asking how they determine the full extent of damage—do they open adjacent walls or floors, inspect framing, and check for active leaks before closing anything back up? Clarify whether the contractor handles minor mold cleanup in-house or brings in a licensed remediation company for larger or more serious contamination. Ask what safety measures they use to contain spores, such as plastic barriers, negative air, and protective equipment. Request detailed photos and written descriptions of all affected areas. Before any repair work begins, ask for a line-item estimate as a change order, showing labor, materials, and any specialty services. Confirm whether materials like old flooring, mastic, or insulation need testing for asbestos or other hazards before removal. Ask what repairs are necessary to satisfy local building codes and pass inspection, for example replacing rotted framing, adding proper waterproofing, or upgrading ventilation. Insist that all corrective work is documented in writing, including what was removed and what was installed in its place. These records are valuable for future buyers, insurance questions, and your confidence that the problem was truly fixed, not just covered over.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ask how the contractor identifies the extent of water damage and mold, whether they bring in a remediation specialist, how repairs will be documented, how costs are estimated, and whether any materials need testing. Request photos and written change orders before proceeding with hidden-damage work.
